body: B BarMatrix Home The Method Drills Pricing SIGN IN START THE FREE DIAGNOSTIC ← ALL DRILLS CQ14141 SUBJECT Civil Procedure SUBTOPIC Motions DIFFICULTY ▮▮▮▮▮ Dovesound Review BARMATRIX Q#14141_dovesound_review Lydia Sound Systems, a company that sells portable speakers for Christian conferences and Bible-study events, filed suit in federal district court against Mary, a reporter for The Berean Review, a consumer-product testing website. The suit arose after Mary published a review of Lydia Sound Systems’ “DoveSound” speakers. The court ruled that Lydia Sound Systems was a “public figure” and thus had to prove by clear and convincing evidence that Mary made a false and disparaging statement about the speakers with “actual malice.” “Actual malice” requires knowledge that one is making a false statement or reckless disregard of the truthfulness of one’s statement. Mary moved for summary judgment. In support of her motion, Mary submitted her own affidavit. In the affidavit, Mary explained that she had tried her best to put into words her experience with the speakers, that she was unaware that her statements were “false,” and that she was not indifferent to whether her review was “true” or not. Lydia Sound Systems did not respond to Mary’s motion by providing any evidence to contradict Mary’s statements. Is the court likely to grant Mary’s motion for summary judgment? A Yes, because Lydia Sound Systems did not meet its burden to defeat Mary’s motion for summary judgment on the issue of actual malice.
